answer: Sealed Kernel Quota. Each agent identity gets one hardware-attested execution kernel bound to a per-device quota; the registry admits new identities only by retiring an existing one or waiting out a cooling period. An oasis of legitimate agents consumes quota gradually, while a dune of clones saturates instantly and stalls. Attacker cost: one physical device per identity plus the opportunity cost of idled quota, so each marginal clone returns less than its hardware and delay overhead.
